title: MAMMO-LENS
subtitle: Mammogram classification with global and local evidence

references.title: A curated mammography data set for use in computer-aided detection and diagnosis research
references.method: Curated DDSM cases with pathology, mass/calcification annotations and breast-density descriptors.
references.use: Defines the dataset and label provenance. Our audited Kaggle JPEG subset differs from the original DICOM collection.
references.limit: Selected abnormal cases support retrospective classification. Future outcomes and screening prevalence require other data.

references.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
references.method: Residual connections ease optimization of deep image networks. The paper evaluates natural-image recognition.
references.use: Provides the ResNet family used for our planned ImageNet-initialized ResNet18 encoder.
references.limit: Natural-image benchmark success does not establish mammography performance.

references.title: Attention-based Deep Multiple Instance Learning
references.method: Learns a permutation-invariant attention operator for bags of instances, with experiments including histopathology.
references.use: Provides gated attention for pooling selected patch embeddings.
references.limit: Different tissue/task and data. Attention weights do not establish causal or clinical explanations.

references.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
references.method: Studies probability calibration and evaluates temperature scaling on image and document classification.
references.use: Motivates fitting one temperature using validation predictions and evaluating probability quality separately.
references.limit: Calibration must be re-evaluated under dataset or image-quality shift.

references.title: Deep Learning to Improve Breast Cancer Early Detection on Screening Mammography
references.method: Uses annotated patches to initialize an all-convolutional whole-image classifier, with DDSM development and INbreast transfer.
references.use: Establishes prior patch-to-image mammography learning and motivates a controlled local/global comparison.
references.limit: Its annotations, cohort and transfer protocol differ from our experiment. Headline scores are not comparable.

references.title: An interpretable classifier for high-resolution breast cancer screening images utilizing weakly supervised localization
references.method: GMIC combines a lightweight global network, saliency-selected high-resolution patches, gated attention and fusion on NYU screening mammograms.
references.use: Closest architectural precedent. It motivates retaining local detail and explicitly crediting existing fusion and attention techniques.
references.limit: Our current patches come from a 256-square image and use texture selection. We cannot claim equivalent localization or clinical validation.

slides.title: MAMMO-LENS
body: Mammogram classification with global and local evidence
Review 1: Proposal and literature
CAI3400 Image Processing and Analysis
Presidency University, Bengaluru
5 November 2026
slides.notes: Good morning. MAMMO-LENS is a research workbench for retrospective benign versus malignant mammogram classification. The central question is whether combining whole-image context with local patches remains reliable across breast-density categories and image degradation. Today I will explain the proposal, its literature basis, our dataset safeguards and completed preliminary baselines.

slides.title: Problem and scope
body: Small image details can disappear during resizing.
A single overall score can hide density and image-quality failures.
Task: benign versus malignant pathology on selected abnormal mammograms.
Research question: does global/local fusion improve classification and reliability?
slides.notes: The task is classification of existing findings from pathology labels. It does not estimate a person's future cancer risk. Our current 256 by 256 working resolution may discard small calcifications, so this is a measurable design limitation. We want to compare feature approaches under the same patient split, then inspect density subgroups, probability quality and performance when images degrade. The dataset does not represent a general screening population.

slides.title: Literature foundation
slides.notes: The dataset paper by Lee defines provenance and annotations. He provides residual encoders. Ilse provides attention pooling for bags of patches, while Guo motivates probability calibration. These are established components. Our implementation combines them for a controlled research experiment. Their original datasets and tasks differ, so none of their reported scores can substitute for our own evaluation. References and links are included at the end and in the proposal.

slides.title: Closest mammography work and proposed focus
body: Li Shen et al.: annotated patch learning transferred to whole images [5].
Yiqiu Shen et al.: GMIC combines global context, selected patches and fusion [6].
Our proposed focus: density subgroup performance and selective prediction under blur/noise.
Novelty remains a hypothesis. Fusion and attention already have strong prior work.
slides.notes: The closest precedent is GMIC, which already uses global and local information plus gated attention. Therefore I would not claim that combining patches and a whole image is a new architecture. Our project focuses on whether any benefit survives density variation and controlled degradation on a strictly audited cohort. Our texture-selected patches are also much simpler than GMIC's learned saliency and high-resolution patches. A positive or negative result is useful if the comparison is reproducible.

slides.title: Audited CBIS-DDSM cohort
slides.notes: We downloaded the Kaggle JPEG export and map case-description series identifiers to JPEGs through dicom_info. The audited cohort contains 2,955 full mammograms from 1,554 patients. Labels are malignant if any described lesion is malignant; both benign categories map to zero. We found no missing mapped JPEGs. We excluded 64 training views from patients appearing in the official test cohort, and all 84 members of 42 duplicate-content groups. Density is known for 2,953 images. These exclusions mean our results use a declared derived cohort rather than an unchanged official benchmark.

slides.title: Patient partitions and leakage controls
slides.notes: Training has 1,740 images from 905 patients. Validation has 578 images from 302 patients. The held-out official test subset has 637 images from 347 patients. There is zero patient overlap across partitions. We use seed 42, fit preprocessing statistics for the classifier on training features, fit temperature only on validation scores, and never use test scores for checkpoint selection. Test results already exist for the handcrafted baselines, so future method changes based on these observations must be acknowledged as exploratory and ultimately need a fresh external evaluation.

slides.title: Methodology and planned deep model
body: JPEG normalization at percentiles 1 and 99.5
Whole image at 256 square pixels
Global features and four texture-selected 64-square patches
Handcrafted logistic regression or shared ResNet18 embeddings
Gated patch attention, feature fusion and optional predicted-density input
Validation calibration, held-out evaluation and browser evidence viewer
slides.source: Encoder [2], attention [3], calibration [4]. Deep experiments pending.
slides.notes: The completed handcrafted baseline extracts intensity histograms, summary statistics and gradients. Patch features pool four regions selected by intensity variation with background filtering. The implemented deep model resizes the global image to 224 square and the selected patches to 128 square before ResNet18 encoding. Gated attention pools patch vectors. A density head provides auxiliary supervision, and the density-conditioned variant consumes predicted density probabilities at inference. Real deep training remains unfinished. Patch selection after heavy downsampling is a major limitation that the next experiments should address.

slides.title: Preliminary real-data baseline results
slides.notes: These are completed real CBIS-DDSM runs, not synthetic smoke scores. Global AUROC is approximately 0.625, patch-only 0.591 and combined 0.620 on the same 637 test images. Global has the lowest Brier score of the three. The intervals overlap, and we have not performed a paired significance test. The correct conclusion is that these preliminary handcrafted features have not demonstrated a fusion improvement. We will keep these baselines as references when evaluating the deep variants.

slides.title: Reliability findings motivate the next experiments
body: Global baseline density-4 AUROC: 0.4895 across 113 test images.
Added noise with standard deviation 0.05 yields zero sensitivity at threshold 0.5.
Global baseline Brier score rises from 0.2359 to 0.3969 under noise.
Higher confidence does not consistently reduce error at very low retained coverage.
slides.source: Local real-baseline-global/metrics.json. Perturbations apply at the 256-square working resolution.
slides.notes: The density-4 result is a subgroup observation, not proof of a clinical density effect. It could reflect sample composition, resolution or model weakness. Under deterministic added noise, all images receive a benign thresholded prediction, although ranking AUROC is still above one half. This shows why accuracy or confidence alone is inadequate. We will assess coverage versus error and choose any abstention policy on validation data. The noise and blur tests are controlled perturbations, not validated simulations of scanner acquisition.

slides.title: Experiment plan and evaluation
body: Compare deep global, patch-only, combined and predicted-density fusion on the frozen cohort.
Hold seed, training budget and selection rule constant across variants.
Report AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, Brier score and patient-cluster intervals.
Evaluate density categories, clean/blur/noise pairs and coverage versus error.
Inspect patch-masking score changes and failure cases.
slides.notes: The initial deep configuration uses ImageNet-initialized ResNet18 with a frozen encoder, ten epochs and batch size eight on the local RTX 4050. We will confirm runtime after improving preprocessing. Validation log loss selects the checkpoint. For calibration we will compare raw and calibrated probabilities, and define operational thresholds on validation data. Patient-level maximum scores are a separate exploratory endpoint. Masking is a response test of the whole pipeline because it recomputes selected patches, not a causal explanation.

slides.title: Progress and review milestones
body: Completed: local frontend/API, audited dataset and three real handcrafted baselines.
Implemented, awaiting real results: ResNet18 fusion, density head and calibration pipeline.
By 17 November: preprocessing optimization, deep comparisons and measured progress review.
By 27 November: full evaluation, error analysis, final report and demonstration.
slides.notes: The local software foundation and real baselines are complete. The previous session passed fifteen automated tests. A CUDA-capable environment is configured, but the interrupted deep run saved no checkpoint. The immediate engineering task is caching deterministic preprocessing and adding robust checkpoint resume so long runs are practical. The next review is listed for 17 November and the final review for 27 November in the project plan. These are work targets, and faculty or LMS instructions remain the scheduling authority.

slides.title: Expected contribution and limitations
body: Deliver a reproducible comparison with patient-level leakage controls.
Measure when density and image quality change model reliability.
Current limits: low working resolution, heuristic patches and one dataset.
Deep-model benefit, clinical utility and external generalization remain unestablished.
slides.notes: The contribution we aim to defend is an auditable experiment that connects image evidence to measured reliability. The current results already show that extra local features can fail to improve held-out performance. The work is retrospective and research only. We need higher-resolution experiments and external validation before making broader claims. I welcome feedback on the experimental scope and the proposed evaluation priorities.
